super_categories.name: Boundary-Aware Actions
super_categories.description: Actions where the agent detects, communicates, or manages the limits of its knowledge, role, or capabilities. Distinct from Decision-Making (action selection) and Communication (general output).

leaves.examples_raw:
Determine whether an incoming query falls outside the agent's role knowledge or capability scope.
"recognize and refuse queries that conflict with their role knowledge" (P22)

Respond to the query with proactive identity disclosure to bound expectations.
"identity disclosure, S2S systems often proactively mention that they are intelligent assistants, which undermine the premise of Turing test" (P11)
"appropriately reject queries that exceed their knowledge boundaries or conflict with their role settings" (P22)
"providing clear refusal responses with appropriate explanations" (P22)

Identify and surface false premises embedded in an incoming query.
"Evaluating whether the model recognizes potential errors in the query" (P22)

super_categories.name: Role Conditioning Actions
super_categories.description: NEW category. Actions by which agents take on, maintain, or leverage domain-expert personas to shape how they process and generate output at inference time. These actions change the framing lens of the agent without modifying model parameters.

leaves.examples_raw:
Role-condition the agent with a domain identity (e.g., Physician, Cardiac Surgeon, Qualitative Researcher) at prompt invocation time to bias its analytical perspective toward domain-specific patterns.
"A pool of k=4 role-conditioned GPT-4o agents are each given the full interview transcript as input" (P27)

Maintain a domain-expert lens through downstream processing steps to produce perspective-diverse outputs alongside identity-neutral agents.
"others may retain role-specific perspectives to support diverse theme formulation" (P27)
"maintain its role-playing ability even when refusing to answer" (P22)
